You are the R7 worker for the Fortress clean-ladder rebuild. You own exactly one rung: R7 — verify the build and full test suite on JDK 25. Expected: ZERO source changes; the deliverable is an empty verification-record commit (same pattern as R4). Work in the clean worktree /home/user/fortress-clean (branch clean-ladder; shares .git with /home/user/fortress).

## Step 0 — verify the tip (STOP if it differs)
cd /home/user/fortress-clean && git log --oneline -1
Expected tip: 4d00c4738 "Upgrade Scala 2.12.20 to 2.13.18 (rung R6)". Anything else → STOP and report.
Confirm `git status --short` is empty before starting.

## Reference
- `864383af4` — the first-ascent JDK 25 commit. Inspect `git show 864383af4 --stat` and the diff to confirm what (if anything) it changed; expected content-free for this branch (the -Xfuture landmine was removed at B5). If it carries real changes that apply here, STOP and report before applying anything.

## Environment (inline on EVERY ant command)
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 && export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH && export FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-clean && unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS && cd /home/user/fortress-clean && ant <target>

## Gate (JDK 25, full)
1. `ant clean compileAll` (~1–2 min)
2. `ant testFast` (~7–9 min) — SUMS must be exactly 1,377 tests / 47 suites / 0 failures / 0 errors
3. `ant testSystem` (~3–4 min) — SUMS must be exactly 382 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors
4. `git status --short` EMPTY after all runs.

Long-suite pattern: redirect each run to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/ prefix r7- (r7-compile.log, r7-testfast.log, r7-testsystem.log), run in background, wait for completion, grep/tail summary lines only — NEVER cat whole logs. Note any new warnings (e.g. javac obsolete-source warnings are expected and stay until R8).

If ANY test fails: do not retry-loop, never skip/quarantine/disable tests. Diagnose briefly, STOP, report verbatim.

## Commit (after the gate is green)
Empty commit recording the verification, R4-style — look at `git show d4698e811` (the R4 verification commit) and match its message style. Subject like "Verify the full gate on JDK 25 (rung R7)". Body: what was verified, gate numbers (compileAll/testFast/testSystem times and sums), note on remaining javac warnings, and note that the first ascent (864383af4) also needed no source changes here. `git commit --allow-empty`. END the message with exactly this footer (last two lines, verbatim):

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX

Never put any model identifier anywhere in the commit.

## Push and checklist
1. `git push origin clean-ladder` — plain fast-forward only, NEVER force. Rejected → STOP and report.
2. Tick the R7 line: in /home/user/fortress (branch claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr), edit explorations/rebuild-plan.md checklist (~lines 468–490): `[ ] R7 JDK 25` → `[x]` with new SHA and gate numbers in the R2–R6 style. Commit (same footer, subject "Tick R7 (JDK 25) in the rebuild checklist") and `git push -u origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`.
3. NEVER push to main.

## Final report
Raw facts for the coordinator: new SHA, parent, confirmation the commit is empty, gate numbers, any new warnings on JDK 25, deviations (or "zero deviations"), push results, surprises.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X".
